rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Wildlife strikes, including bird strikes, are a significant threat to aircraft and can cause aircraft damage or an accident.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Wildlife and bird strikes are reportable aviation occurrences through the CAA occurrence-reporting system.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: The CAA reporting interpretation includes strikes with or without damage, suspected bird strikes and encounters with flocks.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: CAP 772 guides aerodrome operators in establishing and maintaining an effective Bird Control Management Plan.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Bird-strike risk assessment and control should form part of an aerodrome's safety-management system and safety culture.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Aerodrome habitat and surrounding land should be managed to reduce attractiveness to hazardous wildlife.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Aerodrome safeguarding may include regular wildlife patrols and monitoring beyond the airfield where appropriate.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: CAA bird-strike data are aggregated reported occurrences and should not be interpreted as showing that an airport with more reports is necessarily more hazardous.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: Bird-strike risk depends on species, flock size, season, habitat, aerodrome operations, aircraft type, flight phase and reporting practices.

rows.source: CAA wildlife and bird-strike risk management
rows.verified: CAA bird-strike evidence is aerodrome-, species-, aircraft-, operation-, event- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: ORR requires railway dutyholders to manage risks to the public from criminal behaviour, including trespass and vandalism.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: Trespass is a major cause of deaths to members of the public on Britain's railways.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: Vandalism, including placing obstructions on the track, can cause damage, injury or derailment.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: Railway infrastructure controllers must take reasonably practicable steps to prevent unauthorised access.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: Lineside materials should be controlled so they cannot readily be used in acts of vandalism.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: The Railway Safety (Miscellaneous Provisions) Regulations create a goal-setting duty to prevent unauthorised access to railway infrastructure.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: The type of boundary control needed should reflect factors such as vehicle speed, electrification, population density and history of trespass or vandalism.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: British Transport Police leads on criminal damage and railway-byelaw enforcement, while ORR enforces relevant health and safety duties.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: Rail-trespass risk depends on boundary condition, electrification, train speed and frequency, local population, access history, behaviour and enforcement.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and unauthorised-access control
rows.verified: ORR trespass evidence is location-, infrastructure-, user-, operation-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
